clues: This city in Spain sits on an inner plateau, near the north slopes of a mountain range. Its homes cluster on a bend of a river.
High ground far from the coast shapes the weather here. Summer storms soak the nearby mountains, making this province a damp corner of the wide central plateau.
In nineteen eighty five, the whole old centre of this city won a place on the world heritage list. That honour crowned its long past.
A huge Roman aqueduct still strides across the middle of town. It is one of the three great landmarks the city is famous for.
Its cathedral was one of the last in Europe built in the Gothic style. That grand church is the sight that seals the answer.
